title: Microsoft Teams: invite people to register for events by email
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout, custom-domain restriction, licensing background and control paths match the supplied records and Microsoft documentation. One minor correction remains: the PowerShell reference labels Events policy as preview, while the administrator guidance does not.

Set up a custom domain for event emails (recommended)
For a more professional and reliable communication experience, admins can configure Teams events email notifications to be sent from a verified custom domain instead of Microsoft default addresses.

claims.claim: The sending-domain control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Send email notifications from your domain > Use a custom send-from domain address.

On the Organization profile page, select Send email notifications from your domain.
In the Send email notifications from your domain page, select Use a custom send-from domain address.

claims.quote: This setting is an opt-in setting that allows the Microsoft 365 system administrators to select a verified domain within the tenant.

claims.claim: The smaller-event attendee control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events up to 1k attendees.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, in the Who can attend events up to 1k attendees dropdown list, select one of the following:

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EventAccessType EveryoneInCompanyExcludingGuests restricts smaller-event attendance to users in the organisation.
claims.quote:
To only allow users in your organization to attend events with up to 1,000 attendees created by organizers with this policy, run the following command:
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EventAccessType EveryoneInCompanyExcludingGuests
claims.fix: Add to Governance controls: 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference still labels Events policy as preview, although the admin guidance documents these settings without that label.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/teams/set-csteamseventspolicy, which states 'Note that this policy is currently still in preview.' This qualification covers both printed commands; neither call needs changing.

claims.claim: In the Events app, organisers choose whether registration is enabled while scheduling the event.
claims.quote: While scheduling your event, you can choose to turn registration on or off.

claims.claim: In the Events app, the registration setting cannot be changed after the event is first saved.
claims.quote:
After you save your event, you won’t be able to change this setting.
To modify registration, registration must have been turned on before you first saved the event while scheduling it.
